page: Amazon Web Services c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, backed by 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector and matrix capabilities include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, accompanied by hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The platform achieves top-decile CPU benchmark results, reaching 2631.0 on Geekbench single-core and 24632.0 on multi-core tests, paired with a stress-ng single-core score of 3773.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 80093.82. Memory performance is supported by uncached read bandwidth of 217.54 GB/s and write bandwidth of 128.56 GB/s, enabling strong data throughput across compression workloads, demonstrated by a single-threaded gzip speed of 41.47 GB/s and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 552.92 GB/s. For quantized machine learning workloads, CPU-based LLM inference achieves 43.62 tokens per second during medium 7B model text generation.

Hardware tradeoffs center on storage and memory density. The c8a.8xlarge instance does not include bundled local instance storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached network storage volumes over its 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The dedicated single-thread execution cores offer predictable compute performance free from simultaneous multithreading contention. Delivering top-tier execution speed at a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU footprint, the instance offers strong resource efficiency for CPU-intensive tasks such as software compilation, batch compute pipelines, scientific simulations, video transcoding, and web application serving.

Utilizing the AWS Nitro System, the instance features 64.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The architecture supports AVX-512 instructions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware acceleration. Synthetic and application benchmarks highlight top-tier compute capabilities, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2631.0, multi-core scoring 24632.0, and bzip3 decompression achieving 552.92 GB/s.
